assertions.text: Rule file follows the Description-Incorrect-Correct template (title, description, ## Incorrect, ## Correct)
Description states WHAT the rule enforces and WHY, in imperative language (MUST/NEVER, not 'try to' or 'consider')
Incorrect example shows the plausible `git checkout -- <path>` mistake without a prior `git status`, not a contrived variant
Correct example is the minimal fix of the same scenario (checks status / confirms before discarding), not a rewritten unrelated scenario
Rule body contains no numbered steps or multi-step procedural content
Output states or shows evidence of checking existing rules for redundancy/overlap before finalizing
Output states or shows evidence of validating with /rules-review (or explains why it wasn't run)
